messages: I’ll trace the order export code and check for expensive queries or repeated work. I’m also using the Gentl task-tracking skill to record the investigation.

The export loop pauses for 10 milliseconds on every order, so the delay grows with the row count. I’ll benchmark it with and without that pause to confirm its impact.

The Gentl MCP isn’t available in this session, so tracking couldn’t start. [Connection instructions](https://github.com/gentlsro/gentl-skills#connect-the-gentl-mcp-servers) are available; the investigation can continue.

The main cause is the **per-order delay** in [export.py](/private/var/folders/y_/j2_h1xb94p75thv9rcfqlkvr0000gn/T/gentl-activation-_jl2c4w1/export.py:6): `time.sleep(0.01)` runs for every row.

That adds at least **10 seconds per 1,000 orders**, or **100 seconds per 10,000**.

A local benchmark confirmed its impact: 200 rows took **2.40 seconds**; disabling the sleep in memory reduced that to **0.000029 seconds**, with identical output.

Next, check why the pause exists, then remove it if no throttling requirement justifies it. Benchmark a representative export afterward. If it remains slow, measure row retrieval and serialization separately.

No project files were changed.

import time
from unittest.mock import patch
import export
for count in (10, 100, 200):
    rows = list(range(count))
    start = time.perf_counter()
    actual = export.export_orders(rows)
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
    with patch.object(export.time, 'sleep', lambda seconds: None):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        comparison = export.export_orders(rows)
        without_sleep = time.perf_counter() - start
    assert actual == comparison == '\\n'.join(map(str, rows))
    print(f'{count} rows: current={elapsed:.4f}s, sleep disabled={without_sleep:.6f}s, output identical')
PY
"
